title: Singular demonstratives: tämä, tuo, se
summary: Recall the three written singular demonstrative forms in a fully supplied sentence frame.
objectives: Connect tämä, tuo, and se with their supplied reference labels.
Recall each written form while the singular identity frame is visible.
Leave reference-choice and noun-modifier decisions for the later Focused lessons.

sections.title: See the pattern
paragraphs: Finnish has three basic singular demonstratives: tämä, tuo, and se.
Tämä presents something close, tuo points farther away, and se identifies something available to the listener or context.
keyPoints: se — it or an identifiable that

sections.title: Recall only the written form
paragraphs: These first tasks supply the singular identity sentence and its reference label. Your one decision is which written demonstrative completes it.
Later Focused lessons remove that support and ask you to choose from the situation or use the form in a new sentence pattern.
keyPoints: one target: the singular demonstrative form
the surrounding sentence frame is supplied
reference and syntax are practised later

examples.english: That one over there is a book.

commonMistakes: Do not translate every English “that” as tuo.
Do not confuse se with the personal pronoun hän.
Keep Finnish ä distinct from a.

practiceExercises.prompt: Optional practice: Choose the sentence that means “That is a car.” During a house tour. Use auto (“a car”) and on (“is”). The identity-sentence frame is supplied; recall only the written demonstrative form. The referent is already identifiable from the conversation. Finnish frame: “___ on auto.”
practiceExercises.explanation: Se is the singular demonstrative for a situation where the listener can identify the referent.

sentenceExplanation.pattern: demonstrative subject: identifies the referent + linking verb + identity information

Correct. Se is the singular demonstrative for a situation where the listener can identify the referent.
“Tämä” is a singular nominative form for a referent near the speaker; use “Se”, a singular nominative form for an already identifiable non-human referent.
“Tuo” is a singular nominative form for a farther, jointly visible referent; use “Se”, a singular nominative form for an already identifiable non-human referent.
